note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is. Each record is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only). Oklahoma's November 3, 2026 ballot prints only contested races (26 O.S. 6-102): a candidate with no opponent is elected without appearing on it, and its parties nominate in the June 16 primary and the August 25 runoff. The state and local contests carry the Republican, Democratic and Libertarian parties and independents; judges, city offices and fire protection district boards are printed without a party. No Oklahoma party page that a program may read calls anything an endorsement for a 2026 state or local race, so 'endorsements' is empty. Under 'other_support', with the page's own wording in 'kind' and never to be shown as an endorsement: the Oklahoma Democratic Party's 'Our 2026 Candidates' (statewide offices, State Senate and State House; its federal lines are outside this file), the Payne County Democrats' 'Voting Guide' (its list 'Oklahoma Democratic Candidates'; only names and offices were read, never the biographies), and the Tulsa County Republican Party's '2026 Oklahoma State Candidates' and 'Tulsa County Candidates' (the latter says its Republican nominees are now listed). Every one of these candidates is on the ballot under that party's own label, so a line adds nothing to the party printed on the ballot; no party page read names a candidate for a judge, city or fire district contest. 'election' appears only when the candidate is on a primary list and not on the November list (three Democrats whose seats were settled in the June 16 primary: Ron Stewart, Kristina Gabriel, Aletia Haynes Timmons). The page's 'District 17' for Ed Bolt is matched to the only Senate 17 contest on the November list, the unexpired term. Lines matched although the page spells the name differently keep the page's spelling in 'as_listed' (Merridith for Meredith McGinnis, Jonathon for Jonathan Morales, Jeffery for Jeffrey Perez, Rosie Lynch for Rose Rosie Lynch, Carroll Asseo, Chaunte Gilmore, Hildebrandt for Derrick R. Hildebrant, TJ Marti, and names given without a middle initial or a title such as Rep. or Senator). Read on 2026-10-03 with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt checked first; every page in 'lists' was opened a second time and a record kept only if the page still showed the name (none was lost; the Tulsa County Republican Party's site answered the second visit with 429, so its two pages were read again through the reading tool). Facebook and Threads pages are social media and were not read. The Oklahoma Republican Party's own site answers with a CAPTCHA page and was left alone; see not_read. Things for a person to decide: whether John opens the Oklahoma Republican Party's site in his own browser (news reports found by search, not opened, say its State Committee endorsed Mike Mazzei for Governor, James Taylor for Superintendent and Kevin West for Labor Commissioner before the August 25 runoff; Taylor is not on the November list).
